tools.name: list_jurisdictions
tools.description: List every jurisdiction and body of law in the tree, with how far each record reaches and an example path. Start here.

tools.name: find_provision
tools.description: Find the file path of a provision by its number ("1182", "Art. 16a", "reg 13") or words from its heading ("debtor", "Asylrecht").

tools.name: read_law
tools.description: The text of a provision as it was in force on a date, with the law that last changed it, the next change, and any limit of the record that applies.

tools.name: world_on_date
tools.description: What every jurisdiction in the tree looked like on one date: the last change in force in each, and the next.

tools.name: who_wrote
tools.description: Which law wrote each word (or each line) of a provision as it stood on a date, with a count of words per law.

tools.name: compare_dates
tools.description: How a provision changed between two dates: a word-level diff and the laws that took effect in between.

tools.name: provision_history
tools.description: Every law that changed a provision, oldest first, with its in-force, enacted or made, and published dates.

tools.name: laws_between
tools.description: Every law that took effect between two dates, across all jurisdictions or one, in the order they took effect.

tools.name: search_law
tools.description: Search the text of all the law in force on a date, across every jurisdiction or one. Plain text by default.

tools.name: changes_between
tools.description: Every provision whose text differs between two dates, in every jurisdiction or one, with the laws that changed them.

tools.name: list_provisions
tools.description: Browse a corpus: the provision files under a corpus or folder (for example united-states/federal/usc/title-11), with headings, as in force on a date. For a folder of acts or instruments, by_folder gives one row each with its title and last change; a partial name lists the folders that start with it

tools.name: search_changes
tools.description: Search the record of changes (each commit message: the law, its dates, what it did) rather than the text of the law. For example "temporary", "COVID", "Bundesrat".

tools.name: resolve_citations
tools.description: Read every citation in a piece of text (a brief, a judgment, an email) and resolve each to its provision, with its state on a date: in force or not, the law that last changed it, and the next change.

tools.name: check_precedent
tools.description: For case law: a court applied a provision on the day it decided. Is that text still the text in force (today, or on a date), and if not, which laws changed it and how? Also lists judgments the record holds for the provision.

tools.name: what_else_changes
tools.description: Which provisions rely on, cite or use the definitions of this one, on a date: those that cite it, and those that use a term it defines (for example the provisions that use "debtor in possession"), with the definition's scope ("In this subchapter"). Use it before a text search when asked what depends

tools.name: phrase_history
tools.description: When words came into the law and when they left it, at any date and in every jurisdiction: each change whose added or removed text contains them. Use it for things no longer in force (for example "COVID" in the Grundgesetz).

tools.name: applies_to_case
tools.description: For a case commenced on one date, which later changes to a provision reach it (from any scope the record holds, such as "cases commenced on or after"), and the text that applies to it.

tools.name: law_details
tools.description: The full record of a law's change: its commit message with every trailer (enacted, in force, published, sources, scope), the provisions it changed, and what it did to each one's words (a word diff, or "layout only", or "text moved between provisions"). One call answers "what did this law change"; no

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_changes, resolve_citations · Private data: list_jurisdictions, find_provision, read_law, list_provisions, search_changes, check_precedent, applies_to_case, law_details · Public sink: resolve_citations.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_changes, resolve_citations · Private data: list_jurisdictions, find_provision, read_law, list_provisions, search_changes, check_precedent, applies_to_case, law_details · Public sink: resolve_citations

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
